html:
“Still Summer” is a mixtape full of jazz/electronic/ambient music that evokes the kind of cool, spooky wind and crunchy leaves that I pine for here in Texas when the fall equinox hits and it’s still 99 degrees outside:

I started the tape with the working title “See you in the fall,” which is a phrase I used as a sign-off in my last Friday letter. (Reader Pamela B. responded, “Paraphrased from IG: When people say, ‘See you in the fall’ it takes me a minute to realize they mean Autumn—not the end of civilization.” Indeed!)

But then this morning I was writing in my diary and the words “STILL SUMMER” came out of my brush and I thought, Yeah, that’s more like it.

Not only does it still feel like summer here, a lot of this music is very still. It has a pulse, but maybe not a beat. It’s a message to myself: It’s still summer — be still. No sudden movements yet. Estivate. Play dead if you need to. Like a lizard.

You can listen to the mix on Spotify, Apple Music, or YouTube.
